gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX S5000 kit delivers its full 4,500 W only from the 240 V L14-30R outlet (2,400 W at a 120 V 5-20R, 3,600 W at the TT-30R), accepts only BP5000 expansion batteries and does not work with Anker's Home Power Panel (checked against the cited StormWatts page only; the other results were not opened).
standout_why: Compared against the one cited rival page I could open, StormWatts '5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input' (2026-11-16). It already has per-port solar voltage, current and watt limits for the S5000, DELTA Pro 3, F3800 Plus and Explorer 5000 Plus, panel Voc figures and series/parallel layouts, so solar-port pairing is not new. It gives only total AC output at 120/240 V and has no per-outlet watt limits, no connector types or cables, no expansion-battery rule for the S5000 and no home-panel compatibility. The cited Anker F3800 Plus bundle page covers only the F3800 Plus. The cited EcoFlow bundle page returned HTTP 429 on four tries, and the uncited results (solarwaypoint, solargenreview, outletpowered, theoutageready, powerlockdown, powersized) were not opened, so the gap is verified against StormWatts only.
decides: It confirms the Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2x 400 W kit as the linkable row that clears 4,000 W, with a condition: a single 4,000 W load must be a 240 V appliance on the L14-30R, because Anker caps 120 V at 3,600 W (TT-30R) and 2,400 W (5-20R). Later expansion is BP5000 only, and home tie-in is by transfer switch or inlet box, not Anker's Home Power Panel. It does not flip the pick against the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 + 2x 400 W bundle, because EcoFlow's per-outlet limits could not be opened. Shipping conflict to resolve before the page names a pick: Anker's kit page today says orders placed on or after November 6 ship within 11-12 weeks and the 400 W panel ships separately, while the 'Kits we link' table has this kit as 'ships now'. The BLUETTI Elite 400 kits fit only on battery size (3,840 Wh); their 2,600 W AC is below 4,000 W.

findings.label: Home panel compatibility (maker FAQ)
findings.value: Not compatible with the Anker SOLIX Home Power Panel; connects to a home electrical panel 'via a compatible transfer switch or power inlet box'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S5000 + 400W Bifacial Solar Panel - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Anker's Home Backup Kit add-on was listed at $499.99 on the same page that day.

findings.label: Solar input ports (maker landing page)
findings.value: Solar Panel Input 1: 11-60 V, 17 A max, 1,000 W max; Solar Panel Input 2: 16-165 V, 17 A max, 2,000 W max; 3,000 W solar max
findings.note: Port names on the page: 'High-PV Input Port' and 'Low-PV / Car Input Port'. The same page lists generator input at 4,500 W max for the Anker Smart Generator and for third-party generators. StormWatts already publishes these port limits.

findings.label: Which port takes the kit's two panels (arithmetic)
findings.value: Two in series: 115.2 V open-circuit, which fits only Solar Input 2 (16-165 V). A single panel at 57.6 V sits 2.4 V under Solar Input 1's 60 V ceiling.
findings.source_title: 5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input | StormWatts
findings.note: Arithmetic: 2 x 57.6 V = 115.2 V, using StormWatts's figure for the Anker PS400 (57.6 V open-circuit, 48 V / 8.33 A operating). Anker's US kit page does not name the panel model or give its Voc. StormWatts states this layout already and adds that a single PS400 on port 1 may exceed 60 V in cold weather, so this cell is not new.

findings.label: Compatibility cells the cited rival already states (do not repeat as new)
findings.value: DELTA Pro 3: High-PV 30-150 V / 15 A / 1,600 W, Low-PV 11-60 V / 20 A / 1,000 W, EcoFlow 400W panel 48 V open-circuit. Explorer 5000 Plus: two Low-PV ports of 16-60 V / 10.5 A / 600 W each, and Jackery's FAQ allows no more than two SolarSaga 500 X.
